tasks.short: Keep pension, insurance and savings records in line with the carriers.

today.trigger: A joiner, leaver, life event, contract change or carrier invoice arrives.
steps: Read the change in AFAS Profit or in mail from the employee, the manager or the broker.
Retype the enrolment or change into the pension, insurance or savings portal.
Chase missing start dates, hours or plan choices from the HR Administrator or the manager.
Match the carrier invoice to AFAS deductions in Excel.
Answer the employee and the broker on anything the portal will not take.
drudgery: Retyping the same joiner or leaver into each carrier portal
Ticking invoice lines against payroll deductions
Chasing fields that are already in AFAS
today.time_sinks: Daily portal entry and the month-end invoice match take most of these 193 hours. Broker calls and odd life events are fewer and harder.

lenses.faster: Joiner, leaver, life-event and invoice matching runs from AFAS overnight, so the retyping disappears. Exception review and broker contact stay and should take about half of today's time on this task.
lenses.autonomous: Each AFAS contract change and each carrier file starts the match on written plan rules. Clean rows post through; any change to a deduction, an enrolment or a plan choice waits until the specialist clears it.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift warehouse staff at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get a cited answer on their pension and insurance status while the specialist is off, a group that now waits until morning. If that answer is cheap, more of the 750 shift workers will ask, so the real exception queue grows in peak season.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss retyping joiners into portals or ticking invoices. The work worth keeping is a pension choice around the 2027 scheme change and a broker case that does not fit the rules.
lenses.options: At renewal, two insurer quotes or two readings of the pension change can change which plan the works council is asked to accept. A routine enrolment has one plan under the rules, and extra drafts do not change it.
lenses.altitude: The week becomes an exception queue and broker meetings instead of portal entry. The specialist gains the say on eligibility exceptions against written rules, and the job becomes more expert on the pension changeover and less clerical.
reach: The Bookkeeper's check that a pension or insurer invoice matches enrolled staff, once the specialist learns the accounts-payable fields in AFAS. The bookkeeper still posts the invoice.
The HR Administrator's chase for benefit data on joiners, once the specialist knows which AFAS fields are already filled at hire.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist has to judge incomplete disability and life-event files, tell a worried employee what a pension choice means, and get a broker to accept a case the rules do not cover.
tasks.pattern_why: Enrolment, deduction and invoice checks follow plan rules and can be coded against AFAS and the carrier file, with no model in the regular path. A pension question that is not a data change sits on the same exception queue for the specialist to answer from the fund text.

in_practice.trigger: A nightly AFAS joiner, leaver, contract change or life event, or an inbound carrier file or invoice.
steps: Match AFAS people and deductions to the carrier file on an identifier the privacy rules allow.
Post clean enrolments and deduction changes to the carrier format and to the payroll components.
Park mismatches, missing data and plan choices on one exception queue, with the plan rule attached.
Specialist clears the queue, talks to the broker, and answers pension questions from the fund document.
in_practice.human_gate: Ordinary matches post without a signature. The specialist clears every row that changes a deduction, an enrolment or a plan choice before it goes to a carrier or into payroll.
data_needed: AFAS contract, hours and life-event fields
Carrier enrolment and invoice files
Current plan rules and the pension scheme text
The privacy basis for the identifier used to match
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS dossier when a pay or enrolment field changes, and a SharePoint run log of matches, exceptions and who cleared them, kept at least six months.

evidence.claim: Pensioenfonds Vervoer expects its new pension scheme to start on 1 January 2027.
Works-council consent for a pay system does not apply to a mandatory industry pension fund.
A benefits chatbot has to tell the person it is AI.
That Noordhaven's drivers are in Pensioenfonds Vervoer is not shown by the opened sources.

risks: Health and disability details are special-category data under the AVG. The match file should carry enrolment status, not medical notes.
A wrong pension enrolment is hard to undo once the 2027 scheme has started.
Flex workers' pensions sit with the three agencies. They do not belong in Noordhaven's carrier match.
An out-of-hours answer drafted by a model has to say it is AI, and the works council should hear about that system first.
research_questions: What share of these 193 hours is portal rekeying and invoice matching, and what share is broker or employee conversation a file match does not shorten?
Can each carrier and the pension fund provide a file that matches AFAS on an identifier the AVG allows, and how often is that file late or incomplete?
Which groups are in Pensioenfonds Vervoer, which are in an insured scheme, and which funds already fall outside works-council consent under WOR 27(3)?
Do night-shift staff want a written answer out of hours, and will the works council accept it if a model drafts it and states that it is AI?

tasks.short: Grade a job and place it on the CAO or company scale.

today.trigger: A manager asks for a new or changed role, a vacancy opens, or someone disputes a grade.
steps: Collect the description and talk to the manager, sometimes after a look at the floor.
Score the job in Excel against the company factors or the CAO job list.
Search SharePoint and AFAS for a similar role at another site.
Propose the grade and a salary point to the HR Director or the recruiter.
File the result in Word and update AFAS if it is agreed.
drudgery: Scoring similar jobs again from a blank sheet
Hunting the last grade used at another site
Copying factor notes between Excel and Word
today.time_sinks: Finding a comparable role across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo often takes as long as the scoring itself.

lenses.faster: Blank scoring sheets and comparable-job searches disappear once a draft score is prepared from the description and the nearest jobs. The manager conversation, the floor check and signing the grade stay, and those are about two thirds of today's time because each factor still has to be checked.
lenses.autonomous: A request for a new, changed or disputed role starts one draft score on skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions. The grade reaches AFAS or Recruitee only after the specialist signs it.
lenses.ambitious: Recurring agency roles Noordhaven supervises, such as order picker and reach-truck driver, get a documented comparison with own-staff grades for the first time, because those workers count in the pay report and today exist only in agency portals. If a draft grade is cheap, sites will ask for local variants; a variant is justified only where effort or working conditions differ, such as the Venlo cold store against the Rotterdam dock.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying factor text into Excel. The part worth keeping is the conversation with the warehouse manager about what the job actually is on that shift.
lenses.options: Two readings of effort or working conditions can put the same title in different grades and different offer bands, so the drafts change the salary, not only the writing time. Where the sector CAO already names the job, drafts do not change the classification.
lenses.altitude: The week is floor checks and grade decisions, with the paper score already prepared. The specialist gains the say on whether a draft grade stands, and must write reasons the works council can follow, which is more expert work than maintaining the sheet.
reach: The Recruiter's step of putting a grade on a vacancy in Recruitee, once the specialist knows the offer fields and the rule that the band is shown before negotiation.
The HR Business Partner's first answer on what grade a role sits in, only after the description is agreed, so partners keep absence and performance cases.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist sees the job on the night loading dock or in the cold store, which the description often misses, and is the one who signs the grade. A model must not set pay.
tasks.pattern_why: A job description is messy input, and one draft per factor, with a written reason, is a checkable output inside a fixed request flow. The specialist decides. Jobs the sector CAO already classifies stay in that system, and the open sector regrade is not second-guessed by a company score.

in_practice.trigger: A manager, recruiter or HR business partner asks for a grade on a new, changed or disputed role.
steps: Pull the current description, the CAO classification and the nearest Noordhaven jobs from AFAS and SharePoint.
One model call drafts a score on each of the four factors with a reason tied to that text.
The specialist checks the draft against the floor, the site and the CAO list.
The specialist sets the grade and band, or sends a CAO-covered job back to the sector classification.
The signed grade is written to AFAS and, if a vacancy is open, given to the recruiter as the band to show.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist accepts or changes the draft and signs the reason before any AFAS pay field or Recruitee offer band changes.
data_needed: The description and the manager's account of the work
Site conditions, shift and certificates such as forklift, VCA or food safety from Studytube
The consented factor definitions
The sector CAO job list and the company warehouse scale
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint grade file with the input text, the draft scores, the specialist's decision and reasons, and the date. AFAS stores only the agreed grade.

evidence.claim: On 50 UK university job descriptions, one ChatGPT score per HERA factor exceeded 70 percent agreement with experts. Time was not measured, and the factors were not the Dutch four.
Job evaluation for pay transparency uses skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions, and the works council consents to the system, the criteria and the grouping.
evidence.source: Randstad reading of the pay transparency bill, https://www.randstad.nl/werkgevers/hr-wet-en-regelgeving/actuele-wetgeving/wet-loontransparantie

evidence.claim: If core accountabilities have not materially changed, an AI-related change in the work is not a reason for a one-off regrade.
A pay decision made solely by a model conflicts with GDPR Article 22, and a wrong grade becomes an unexplained pay difference.

risks: A draft copied into pay without a signed decision can breach the ban on a solely automated decision and can create an unexplained gap.
From 2 December 2027 a grade recommendation can be high-risk under AI Act Annex III 4(b), which brings oversight, six-month logs and telling worker representatives first.
CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer parties are still regrading sector jobs, so a company grade can conflict with a result that is not out yet.
The UK pilot used HERA on university jobs. It says nothing yet about Dutch warehouse work.
research_questions: On about 30 Noordhaven jobs, how often does a four-factor draft match the specialist's grade, and how often would a mismatch have changed pay?
Which jobs does CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer already classify, and will the open sector regrade replace a company score?
Does the works council treat a draft inside the current system as ordinary work, or as a new grading system that needs consent under WOR 27(1)(c)?
How often does a cold-store or night-loading job contain facts the paper description misses, enough that the draft is usually wrong?

tasks.short: Review benefit and safety practices and propose policy changes.

today.trigger: An insurer renewal, a broker proposal, a pension or legal change, or a question from the HR Director.
steps: Find the current policy and the last signed terms on SharePoint.
Read the insurer, broker and pension-fund documents.
Rebuild a cost and cover comparison in Excel.
Write a recommendation to the HR Director.
Discuss it with the director and, where consent is needed, the works council.
drudgery: Searching SharePoint for the last signed terms
Rebuilding the same comparison table each renewal
Summarising long fund PDFs by hand
today.time_sinks: Reading conditions and rebuilding the comparison take the hours. The decision meeting is short.

lenses.faster: Hunting old terms and rebuilding the comparison table disappear. Reading the few clauses that drive cost, writing the recommendation and the works-council discussion stay, together about three fifths of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A renewal date, a fund document or a request from the HR Director starts a sourced comparison. The note goes out only after the specialist signs it, and a change to a plan still needs the director and, where WOR applies, the works council.
lenses.ambitious: The works council gets a short comparison of health-insurance choices and the pension changeover before it is asked to consent, instead of a long mail. If that note is cheap, each site will ask for its own version, so the note stays one company decision unless a site's cover really differs.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss searching SharePoint for last year's PDF. The part worth keeping is the judgment on what Noordhaven should change and what it should leave alone.
lenses.options: Two or three cover and contribution options can change what the works council is asked to consent to, and what Payroll will deduct. A single-insurer renewal with no real alternative does not need extra drafts.
lenses.altitude: The week has fewer document searches and more signed recommendations on the HR Director's agenda. The specialist gains the preparation of that agenda and becomes more of a policy adviser on benefits, pension and the safety-related allowances that sit in the CAOs.
reach: The Controller's question on what a benefit change does to the monthly labour cost, once the specialist learns which general-ledger accounts Payroll already uses.

The Learning and Development Specialist's list of who holds a forklift, VCA or food-safety certificate, where that certificate is the condition for an allowance, once the specialist can read Studytube completions.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist has to judge what fits this sector CAO, the company warehouse CAO, three sites and this works council, and has to recommend the change in their own name.
tasks.pattern_why: The comparison steps repeat at each renewal, so an agent is unnecessary, but the product is a policy recommendation the specialist leads. No opened source shows a model that can choose a Dutch logistics benefits change on its own.

in_practice.trigger: A broker renewal, a new pension or insurer document, or a request from the HR Director.
steps: Collect the current SharePoint policy, the last terms and the new document.
Draft a comparison of who is covered, what it costs and what would change in AFAS deductions, with each row tied to a clause.
The specialist cuts anything the source does not say and writes the recommendation.
The HR Director decides what to take to the works council.
Payroll sees a change only after consent, where WOR requires it.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist signs the note before it goes to the HR Director. The director, and the works council where WOR applies, decide any change to the plan.
systems: Excel for the specialist's own edits
data_needed: Current policies and signed terms
Insurer, broker and pension-fund documents
Headcount by site and by own staff versus agency
Any claim or cost totals already in AFAS or Power BI
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint benefits folder: source documents, the signed note, the decision and the date. AFAS changes only after the decision.

evidence.claim: Pensioenfonds Vervoer expects its new scheme on 1 January 2027, which is a dated change the benefits note has to cover if drivers are in that fund.
A pay or grading system needs works-council consent, except where a CAO settles it or for a mandatory industry pension fund.
Compa's analyst agent drafts market-pricing findings from Mercer data, and no customer result is published. It does not compare Dutch benefit plans.
No opened source shows a Dutch employer letting a model choose a benefit-policy change.

risks: A comparison that smooths over a clause can send the works council a choice the insurer will not honour.
Health-plan material is sensitive under the AVG and should stay out of a general prompt history.
A benefit change can be a change to terms that needs consent even when the software change in AFAS looks small.
Site-by-site variants requested because the note was easy to produce can create unequal cover that later shows up in the pay report.
research_questions: In the last two renewals, was the delay in finding and comparing terms, or in the broker and the works council?
Do the insurers already deliver a comparison the specialist accepts, so a draft adds little?
Which benefit changes would the works council refuse to discuss unless the note quotes the policy and the fund text?
Are drivers actually in Pensioenfonds Vervoer, or does the 2027 scheme change miss this workforce?

tasks.short: Explain pay, benefits, the CAO and the rules to managers and staff.

today.trigger: A manager or employee asks by Outlook, Teams or on the floor.
steps: Search the sector CAO, the warehouse CAO and SharePoint policies.
Check the person's contract, scale and site in AFAS.
Reply in writing or call back.
Repeat when another site asks the same allowance question.
Escalate borderline cases to the HR Director.
drudgery: Searching for a clause already used last week
Re-explaining the same shift allowance per site
Waiting until the specialist is in, which delays night supervisors to the next day
today.time_sinks: Lookup is half the work. Night-shift supervisors lose a day because the specialist works days.

lenses.faster: Searching the CAO PDF and SharePoint during the question disappears, because a cited draft is ready first. The conversation and the borderline judgment stay, and those should still take about two thirds of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A question in Outlook or Teams, or a pay question still open as it ages toward two months, starts a draft that cites the clause and the AFAS contract. The specialist sends every answer, and calls when the clause does not decide.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift supervisors get a written answer on shift allowances and scale questions during the shift, a group that now waits until the next day. If answers are cheap, more managers of the 750 shift staff will ask before they promise an allowance, and borderline questions still come to the specialist.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting SharePoint mid-call for an article they have used before. The part worth keeping is the talk in which a manager decides what to do on that shift.
lenses.options: Where the CAO states the allowance, extra drafts do not change the answer. Where the company warehouse CAO is silent, two defensible readings change what the manager is told to pay, and the specialist has to pick one and record it.
lenses.altitude: The week is live advice with the file already open, including a list of pay questions approaching two months. The specialist does not gain a new formal right; they become more expert on borderline CAO cases and less of a memory for every article.
reach: The HR Business Partner's routine answers on scales and allowances where a written clause already decides, so partners keep Wet verbetering poortwachter and manager coaching.
The Recruiter's check that an offer does not ask for salary history and shows the band before negotiation, once the specialist has taught the recruiters that rule.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist reads the manager's real situation, including a promise already made on a night shift, and gives advice that person will follow. A clause citation does not do that.
tasks.pattern_why: The specialist stays the lead because the answer has to fit the person, the site and the shift. The draft is a lookup of the current CAO and the contract inside that conversation, not a case that runs on its own.

in_practice.trigger: A manager or employee asks in Outlook or Teams, or a pay question has been open long enough to risk the two-month reply duty.
steps: Pull the contract, scale, site and employee group from AFAS.
Draft an answer that cites the sector CAO, the warehouse CAO or the SharePoint policy, and quote the clause.
The specialist corrects the draft and sends it, or calls when the text does not decide.
Store the question, the clause and the answer that was actually sent.
Escalate to the HR Director when the two CAOs conflict or the answer would change pay practice.
in_practice.human_gate: Only the specialist sends the answer. If the clause does not decide, the specialist says so and does not let the draft stand as the company's position.
data_needed: The current text of both CAOs and the company policies
The employee's AFAS contract, scale and site
A log of answers already given, so sites do not get contradictions
The date the pay question arrived
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint advice log with the question, the clause, the answer sent and the specialist's name. Pay answers are also noted on the AFAS dossier.

evidence.claim: Employees can request pay information and the employer answers within two months. Salary history is not asked, and the band is shown before negotiation.
evidence.source: Randstad reading of the pay transparency bill, https://www.randstad.nl/werkgevers/hr-wet-en-regelgeving/actuele-wetgeving/wet-loontransparantie

evidence.claim: CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer parties are regrading sector jobs and no outcome is published yet, so advice has to name which text is in force.
A drafted answer is only as reliable as the clause version it cites, and an outdated CAO PDF produces a confident wrong answer.

risks: A draft that cites an old CAO text will be treated as the company line if the specialist is rushed.
The same allowance explained differently at Venlo and Rotterdam becomes an unexplained difference in the later pay report.
Night-shift answers sent unread can confirm a promise a manager has already made.
Pay questions answered late breach the two-month duty once the law is in force.
research_questions: What share of questions are settled by one current clause, and what share need a judgment the clause does not contain?
How often is the CAO PDF on SharePoint older than the text the parties are actually applying?
Will night-shift supervisors write the question, or do they only ask on the floor?
How many pay questions in the last year were answered inside two months, and which were late?

tasks.short: Design and run merit and incentive pay.

today.trigger: The yearly merit round, or a manager asking for a bonus, a certificate allowance or a market correction.
steps: Export pay and any ratings from AFAS to Excel.
Check who is fixed by a CAO and who can still move.
Build a cost scenario and chase missing inputs.
Calibrate with managers and the HR Director.
Rewrite the sheet and hand the result to the Payroll Specialist.
drudgery: Rebuilding the merit workbook each round
Chasing missing ratings and certificate records
Checking CAO minimums row by row
today.time_sinks: The workbook and the chase take longer than the calibration meeting.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding the workbook and chasing CAO minimums by hand disappear once headcount, scale and cost sit in one model. Calibration meetings, scheme design and works-council handling stay, and those are about two thirds of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A merit cycle date or a request for an incentive starts a costed scenario from AFAS, limited to people the CAO does not already fix. Nothing is paid until the HR Director proposes it, the works council consents where WOR requires, and Payroll loads it.
lenses.ambitious: The Recruiter gets a costed 90-day retention incentive for hard-to-fill night warehouse roles, a service they do not get today, tied to people still here and productive at day 90. If costing is cheap, every site will ask for its own scheme, while the CAO and works-council consent limit how many schemes can exist.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the spreadsheet or chasing cells. The part worth keeping is designing a scheme managers will apply fairly, and seeing whether people stay past day 90.
lenses.options: A certificate bonus, a 90-day retention bonus and no scheme at all change who gets paid and what the wage bill does, so the scenarios change the decision. An AI-skill premium is a fourth option only for the small office group, and the evidence on paying it is unsettled.
lenses.altitude: The week is scheme design and calibration, not workbook maintenance. The specialist gains the right to recommend a costed design to the HR Director, and still has no right to pay it; the job becomes more expert on retention and less on spreadsheet upkeep.
reach: The Payroll Specialist's loading of an approved one-off incentive, once the specialist learns the AFAS wage-component sheet Payroll uses. Payroll still runs the month close.
The FP&A Analyst's translation of an approved incentive into the labour-cost forecast, once the specialist uses FP&A's planning assumptions.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist has to choose a scheme shift managers will run fairly, spot two employees the sheet treats as equal when the floor does not, and carry the proposal to the works council. There is no documented Dutch merit cycle a model can run.
tasks.pattern_why: No opened source shows a Dutch merit cycle run by a model. Costing a chosen scheme is a calculation with rules; who is eligible, what the CAO already fixes, and what the works council will accept stay with the specialist.

in_practice.trigger: The planned merit window, or a recruiter or manager request for an incentive on a named hard-to-fill role.
steps: Load headcount, scale, site, CAO coverage and 90-day retention from AFAS, and certificate completions from Studytube.
Cost two or three schemes the specialist has already named, and show who is excluded because the CAO fixes their pay.
The specialist and the managers calibrate, and the specialist writes the proposal.
The HR Director takes it to the works council where WOR 27(1)(c) applies.
After consent, Payroll receives a signed input file, not a model feed.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist does not load a new pay element. The HR Director decides to propose a scheme, and the works council consents unless the CAO already settles it.
systems: Excel for the signed input file
data_needed: Pay elements and CAO coverage by person
90-day retention and offer acceptance by role and site
Studytube completions for forklift, VCA and food safety
Existing works-council agreements on variable pay
Manager ratings, if the company decides ratings are allowed as an input
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint compensation folder: scenarios, the proposal, the consent record and the file sent to Payroll. AFAS holds the paid result.

evidence.claim: No opened page shows a Dutch AI merit cycle.
Of 500 employers in an August 2026 panel, 58 percent pay an AI-skill premium now or within a year, and 23 percent already treat that skill as baseline. The groups overlap, and this is stated intent.
Zapier's idea of extra pay for AI-sourced gains has not run, and any credit would be case by case.
A pay system needs works-council consent except where a CAO settles it.

risks: Copying an AI-skill premium into a warehouse scale would outrun both the evidence and the CAO. Most of the 750 shift roles are not AI-skill jobs.
A scheme managers apply differently on night shift and day shift creates a gap the 2028 report has to explain.
Ratings used as a pay input can be personal data and a high-risk use once pay recommendations fall under the AI Act from 2 December 2027.
Paying without works-council consent, where the CAO does not settle it, is a WOR problem, not a software setting.
research_questions: Which roles have pay fixed by a CAO, and which can still receive a company merit or incentive payment?
Did any past incentive move 90-day retention or offer acceptance on a warehouse role, or only office salaries?
Will the works council consent to a retention or certificate incentive, and does AFAS already have a wage component Payroll can run?
How many employees have an AI-related skill the company would pay for, or is that group too small for a scheme?

tasks.short: Advise on complaints about job grade or salary.

today.trigger: An employee or a manager writes that a grade or a salary is unfair.
steps: Read the complaint and talk to the manager.
Pull the grade, scale and pay history from AFAS.
Find comparators at the same site and at the other sites in Excel.
Meet the employee, often with the HR Business Partner.
Write the outcome and file it.
drudgery: Assembling pay history and comparators by hand
Reconciling different job titles for the same work across three sites
Rewriting the file before every meeting
today.time_sinks: Building the file takes longer than the conversation. Repeat complaints from one site are handled as if each were the first.

lenses.faster: Pulling pay history, the grade and comparators by hand disappears into a prepared file. The hearing, the judgment and the written outcome stay, and those should take about three fifths of today's time because each case still needs to be read.
lenses.autonomous: A written complaint starts a case file: grade, scale, comparators, CAO clause and pay history. The file does not go to the employee until the specialist has decided the recommended resolution and signed it.
lenses.ambitious: The works council gets a twice-yearly pattern of grade and salary complaints by site and job family, which they do not get today, so a repeated Venlo or night-shift issue is visible before a 5 percent unexplained gap triggers a joint evaluation. If that note is cheap they will want it after every case, which would turn single complaints into a running dispute, so it stays on a fixed calendar.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pulling pay lines out of AFAS one by one. The part worth keeping is the fair hearing and a clear answer the employee and the manager can live with.
lenses.options: Three outcomes change the decision itself: the grade stands and is explained, pay is corrected to a real comparator, or the case goes to a joint review with the works council. The specialist chooses; the drafts are the choice, not a writing aid.
lenses.altitude: The week is hearings and signed outcomes, with the file ready. The specialist keeps the decision on the individual case and becomes more expert on equal-pay reasons, and spends less time as a file clerk.
reach: The HR Business Partner's assembly of the team facts before a pay complaint meeting, once the specialist can use the partner's notes. The hearing stays with both of them.
The People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's cut of pay by site and job family for those complaint patterns, once the specialist knows the nightly AFAS extract.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist hears the person, weighs fairness against the CAO and the real job, and stands behind the answer if the works council challenges it. The model does not issue the outcome.
tasks.pattern_why: The case file is most of the hours and can be drafted in one pass from AFAS and the CAO. The advice on how to resolve it stays with the specialist, because this is an individual pay outcome and a wrong grade becomes an unexplained pay difference.

in_practice.trigger: An employee or manager sends a grade or salary complaint, or a pay-information request that is really a complaint.
steps: Build a file from AFAS: grade, scale, site, shift, pay history and comparators in the same job family.
Attach the CAO or company-scale clause and any earlier outcome for that job.
Draft three options with reasons, marked as a draft, not as a decision.
The specialist meets the employee and the manager, decides, and writes the outcome in their own words.
A twice-yearly pattern, with names removed, goes to the HR Director and the works council.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist decides the recommended resolution and signs it before anything is sent. A draft stored on the dossier is labelled as not a decision.
data_needed: The complaint text and the date it arrived
Grade, scale, site, shift and pay history
Comparators with the same work, including agency pay only where the agency has supplied it
The CAO clause and prior outcomes
Works-council status of the grading system
in_practice.logs_to: The employee's AFAS dossier holds the signed outcome only. Drafts and the pattern note sit in a restricted SharePoint folder with access logged, kept at least six months.

evidence.claim: A gap of 5 percent or more that stays unexplained for six months triggers a joint evaluation with the works council. Pay requests are answered within two months.
evidence.source: Randstad reading of the pay transparency bill, https://www.randstad.nl/werkgevers/hr-wet-en-regelgeving/actuele-wetgeving/wet-loontransparantie

evidence.claim: A wrong grade becomes an unexplained pay difference, and a pay decision made solely by a model conflicts with GDPR Article 22.
Grade or pay recommendations can fall under AI Act Annex III 4(b), high-risk from 2 December 2027, with competent oversight, six-month logs and worker representatives told first.

risks: A draft outcome left on the employee dossier looks like a decision made before anyone decided, which is an AVG and Article 22 problem.
Comparators that ignore site, shift or agency status can hide a gap or invent one.
Complaint text is personal data and should not be used to train a general model.
An early pattern report to the works council can turn a single case into a collective dispute if names can be guessed.
research_questions: How many grade and salary complaints arrived in the last year, and how many turned on a missing fact rather than on disagreement with a fair grade?
On past files, how often would the specialist have rejected a draft recommendation?
Does storing a draft in the employee dossier create an AVG problem or look like a decision made before a person decides?
Does the works council want a pattern of complaints, or would that report inflame individual cases?

tasks.short: Write job descriptions, classifications and salary scales.

today.trigger: A new role, a reorganisation, a CAO change, or a scale that no longer matches the work.
steps: Interview the manager and look at similar descriptions in Word.
Draft the description and a classification note.
Build or edit the salary scale in Excel.
Check the title against the sector CAO and the warehouse CAO.
Save versions to SharePoint, AFAS and, if hiring, Recruitee, and reconcile them when they drift.
drudgery: Formatting the same description structure again
Keeping Word, Excel, AFAS and Recruitee on the same numbers
Rewriting a day-shift description with 'night' typed on top
today.time_sinks: Aligning the four places the scale lives takes as long as writing the description.

lenses.faster: First drafts, scale formatting and copying the same numbers into four systems disappear. Manager interviews, edits to effort and working conditions, and publishing one signed version stay, and those are about half of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A request for a new or changed description starts a draft from the manager's notes and the nearest signed job. The description and the scale are published only after the specialist releases them, and recruiters can show only that band.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift team leaders, whose work is often an edited day-shift description, get their own description and scale placement for the first time. If drafting is cheap, managers will ask for a new description whenever tasks drift, including planning jobs that now use software, and those requests go ahead only when core accountabilities have changed.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss formatting tables and reconciling four copies of the scale. The part worth keeping is a description a warehouse team lead recognises as their job, and a scale the company can defend.
lenses.options: Two drafts that stress different factors can change the grade and the band shown to a candidate, so the wording is the decision. Breakpoints on the scale change offer salaries, not only the look of the table.
lenses.altitude: The week is editing and agreeing descriptions with managers, then releasing one version. The specialist gains the say on which text recruiters must use, and becomes more expert on the job architecture and less on document upkeep.
reach: The Recruiter's editing of vacancy text in Recruitee so it matches the graded description and carries the band before negotiation.
The People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's upkeep of job categories in the nightly extract, once the specialist learns those AFAS fields and keeps them as the single list.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist tests the draft with a team lead who knows the work, decides the scale the company will defend, and refuses a cosmetic rewrite that would create a pay difference.
tasks.pattern_why: The description and the factor reasons are one checkable draft from messy manager input. Scale points that follow from an agreed grade are a formula afterwards. The specialist decides the grade before either is published, and CAO-covered jobs keep the sector classification.

in_practice.trigger: A manager or recruiter asks for a new description, or a signed description no longer matches the work.
steps: Collect the manager's notes, the current description and the nearest signed jobs.
One model call drafts the description and a reason on each of the four factors, flagged where the text is thin.
The specialist rewrites it with the team lead, especially effort and working conditions.
The scale row is calculated from the signed grade and the current CAO or company table.
One released version is written to SharePoint and AFAS, and Recruitee vacancies use that band.
in_practice.human_gate: The specialist publishes the description and the scale. Recruiters cannot show a band that has not been released. A change to the factors or the scale structure waits for works-council consent.
data_needed: Manager and team-lead account of the work, by site and shift
Current scales and CAO classifications
AFAS job-scheme fields
Open vacancies in Recruitee that would inherit the band
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint version history with the draft, the edits, the specialist's release and the date. AFAS stores the released job and grade.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as preparation for pay transparency. Those are fields, not a model.
One ChatGPT score per HERA factor on 50 UK job descriptions exceeded 70 percent agreement with experts. Time was not measured.
In an August 2026 panel, 61 percent of employers are rewriting job descriptions for AI, 49 percent say salary structures lag, and 48 percent say benchmarks miss AI skills.
If core accountabilities have not materially changed, do not run a one-off regrade because the tools around the job changed.

risks: A fluent draft that the team lead has not checked will misstate cold-store effort or night working conditions and then set pay.
Four systems will drift again if Recruitee or Excel keeps a private copy of the band.
A local description for a job the sector CAO is regrading can conflict with the outcome still to come.
Changing the scale structure without works-council consent breaches WOR 27(1)(c) where the CAO does not settle it.
research_questions: How much of a draft description do warehouse team leads rewrite, especially the lines on effort and working conditions?
Can AFAS Profit job schemes hold the band recruiters must show before they negotiate, or does the band still live in Excel?
For which titles does the sector CAO already fix the classification, so a local description would conflict?
Do night-shift team-lead jobs differ in accountabilities from day-shift leads, or only in hours?

tasks.short: Cost pay scenarios for CAO talks and for management.

today.trigger: A CAO round, a pension-rate change, or the HR Director asking what a proposal costs.
steps: Pull headcount and pay from AFAS or the nightly Power BI extract into Excel.
Apply wage tables, shift allowances and employer charges by hand.
Add a pension assumption and a rough flex-hours figure.
Make two or three versions because formulas break.
Explain the total to the HR Director and check it with Payroll or the Controller.
drudgery: Rebuilding formulas each round
Reconciling the extract to Payroll's last close
Re-typing allowance rules that have not changed
today.time_sinks: The model is rebuilt more often than it is used. Tying it back to the last payroll close is the long part.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding the workbook disappears. Setting assumptions, tying the total to the last payroll close and explaining the pack stay, and those should take under half of today's time.
lenses.autonomous: A CAO proposal, a pension-rate change or a request from the HR Director starts a cost run from the nightly AFAS extract and the written wage rules. Each pack is released only after the specialist checks it against Payroll's last close.
lenses.ambitious: The HR Director gets the cost of a CAO proposal and of the January 2027 pension change in the week the proposal appears, a decision that today waits on a rebuilt spreadsheet. If a run is cheap, what-ifs from FP&A and the sites will multiply, so only proposals that change the wage bill are released.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pivoting the same headcount extract and repairing formulas. The part worth keeping is judging which proposal the company can afford and explaining that to the director.
lenses.options: An across-the-board percent, a higher shift allowance and a one-off payment change what management can agree in CAO talks, so the scenarios are the decision. Extra runs that do not move the wage bill do not need a new pack.
lenses.altitude: The week is reviewing and releasing scenario packs rather than building them. The specialist gains the say on which pack the HR Director may use, and becomes more expert on which assumptions move the bill, including pension and flex hours.
reach: The FP&A Analyst's wage-round version of the labour budget, once the specialist states assumptions FP&A already uses and the pack ties to the last close.
The Controller's test that a people-cost scenario still matches payroll, once the specialist learns the month-close tolerance the Controller already applies.

tasks.human_edge: The specialist chooses assumptions negotiators can stand behind, spots a total that cannot be right against last year's payroll, and refuses a precise number where the sector regrade or the pension rate is still a range.
tasks.pattern_why: CAO wage tables, allowances, employer charges and pension rates are rules and can be coded against the AFAS extract, with no model needed for the arithmetic. Interpretation of a proposal, and any market-pay finding, stays with the specialist before a pack is released.

in_practice.trigger: A written CAO proposal, a published pension contribution change, or a request from the HR Director for a cost.
steps: Refresh headcount, scale, site, allowances and flex hours from the nightly AFAS extract and agency hour files.
Run the named scenarios through the wage, employer-charge and pension rules.
Compare the base case to Payroll's last close and flag any component that misses the agreed tolerance.
The specialist reads the assumptions, including anything still unknown because the sector regrade has no outcome.
The specialist releases the pack to the HR Director or holds it.
in_practice.human_gate: Every pack used outside the specialist's working file is signed off by the specialist. Unreleased runs are not quotes for bargaining.
data_needed: Payroll totals by wage component for the last close
Current CAO tables and the company warehouse scale
Pension contribution rates, or a stated range if the 2027 rate is not final
Agency hours and, when supplied, agency pay
FP&A's labour-budget assumptions
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint costing log: extract date, rules version, assumptions, tolerance result, who released the pack, and to whom.

evidence.claim: CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer parties are regrading sector jobs and no outcome is published, so a cost model can go stale in one round.
Pensioenfonds Vervoer expects its new scheme on 1 January 2027, which changes employer pension cost if Noordhaven's drivers are in it.
Agency workers count in the pay-transparency report, and agencies supply their pay data.
evidence.source: Randstad reading of the pay transparency bill, https://www.randstad.nl/werkgevers/hr-wet-en-regelgeving/actuele-wetgeving/wet-loontransparantie

evidence.claim: Compa with Mercer data drafts market-pricing findings and publishes no customer result. It does not cost a Dutch CAO proposal.

risks: A pack that does not tie to Payroll's last close will be used in talks and then fall apart.
The sector regrade has no outcome yet, so a single precise total overstates what is known.
Leaving out agency hours understates the labour picture the transparency report still has to cover.
Cheap extra scenarios will be quoted as the company's position if unreleased runs leave the working file.
research_questions: Can a rule-based model reproduce last year's payroll total by component within a tolerance Payroll and the Controller accept?
How many scenarios did the last CAO round actually use, and would more scenarios have changed the mandate?
What part of the model breaks when the sector regrade lands, and is the 2027 pension contribution known as a number or only as a range?
Will the three agencies provide hours and pay in time for a pack, or only after their own invoices?

role.altitude: From grading jobs one by one and retyping carrier files, to owning the job architecture and the evidence behind every pay difference the company may have to explain.
reach: The Payroll Specialist's loading of an already agreed wage-table or allowance change into AFAS, once the specialist can use payroll's wage components and the month-close calendar. Payroll still closes the month.
The People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's pull of the pay comparison for own staff and agency workers from the nightly AFAS extract, once the specialist knows those fields.
The Recruiter's placement of the approved band on the Recruitee offer before salary negotiation, and the drop of any salary-history question.
The FP&A Analyst's translation of a wage or pension scenario into the labour-cost forecast, once the pack uses FP&A's assumptions and ties to the last payroll close.
The HR Business Partner's routine answers on scales and allowances where a written clause already decides, so business partners keep absence, return to work and manager coaching.
role.ceiling_note: This is one person at a loaded EUR 75 an hour. These eight tasks are a bit over half the role; talks with the works council, brokers and CAO parties fill much of the rest and do not shrink the same way. The sector CAO fixes most transport pay and is mid-regrade, the company warehouse CAO and works-council consent fix how fast any new scale or incentive can move, and agency pay for 150 to 300 flex workers depends on three staffing firms. The pension change on 1 January 2027, the report on 2027 pay due by 7 June 2028, and high-risk duties from 2 December 2027 if grade or pay recommendations are in use, add work before they remove any.
skills_to_grow: Score jobs on skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions, and write reasons the works council can follow.
Read AFAS wage components, job schemes and the nightly extract well enough to tie a pack to Payroll's close.
Measure an unexplained pay gap by site, job family and own staff versus agency, using data the agencies actually supply.
Check a pension or insurer answer against the fund text and the policy, including the 2027 scheme if drivers are in Pensioenfonds Vervoer.
Keep a log of grade and pay recommendations that shows the draft, the human decision and the date, fit for a later AVG or AI Act question.
role.ambitious_version: This specialist keeps one job architecture for Noordhaven's own staff and a documented pay comparison for agency workers, so every offer shows a band before negotiation and every pay question is answered inside two months with a reason. The HR Director gets a costed CAO and pension scenario before bargaining and before the January 2027 scheme change. Offer acceptance and 90-day retention are read against unexplained gaps by site, job family and own staff versus agency, in time for the report on 2027 pay due by 7 June 2028.
